subject: Reserved capacity tenor and start-window — sizing & SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Emma Reynolds <emma.reynolds@aurorasoft.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity tenor and start-window — sizing & SLA tradeoffs

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Per our discussion attached is the pricing deck (Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_v2.pdf) and a short note on tradeoffs between a 12/24/36-month reserved commit for a Dedicated GPU pool. A few items we want to confirm to make the proposal tight for Aurora: 

- Baseline throughput target: you mentioned ~120 rps sustained for the headline model with spiky peaks to 320 rps. Is that still accurate?
- Desired start window: you said "early Nov" — can you confirm an exact target (Nov 1 vs Nov 15)?
- Ramp tolerance: do you want a phased ramp (staging buffer) or a straight start-to-capacity?

High-level framing: shorter tenors (12) give you flexibility but lower discounts; longer tenors (36) unlock >25% list discount and committed GPU reservations. We can offer a hybrid: 24-month with a graded ramp schedule and a small staging buffer for the first 60 days.

If you can confirm the throughput & target start date I’ll get a commercial term note back to you and cc legal/procurement for invoice schedule.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_v2.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

From: Emma Reynolds <emma.reynolds@aurorasoft.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@aurorasoft.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tenor and start-window — sizing & SLA tradeoffs

Irene —

Thanks for the deck. Quick clarifications so we can route to procurement:

- Throughput: yes, roughly 120 rps sustained. Peaks are traffic-driven; we need headroom to 300–320 rps for short bursts (<= 3–5 minutes).
- Start date: target Nov 15 to align with our Q4 feature launch. If an earlier date (Nov 1) materially reduces cost, we could consider.
- Ramp: we prefer a phased ramp with a small staging buffer (20% of committed capacity) for the first 90 days. That reduces risk while we shift traffic.

Procurement asks: can you include a proposed SLA credit schedule if we miss throughput/latency guarantees? Also we need invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether you can provide a mid-term option to increase capacity without re-negotiating the term.

Looping in procurement for budget note.

—Emma
Emma Reynolds
Head of Platform Engineering, AuroraSoft
emma.reynolds@aurorasoft.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Emma Reynolds <emma.reynolds@aurorasoft.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tenor and start-window — sizing & SLA tradeoffs

Emma —

Appreciate the clear targets. Quick technical/commercial framing from our side to help procurement:

1) GPU pool sizing: for 120 rps sustained with 300 rps short bursts, our recommendation is:
   - Primary pool: 6x A800-class GPUs (optimized for inference) providing sustained throughput headroom.
   - Burst pool: automated autoscale to add up to 3x additional GPUs for short durations; we charge bursting at a slightly higher per-hour rate but do not require a long-term commit for burst capacity.

2) Throughput guarantees & SLA:
   - We provide a 99.5% availability SLA for inference endpoints across the Dedicated pool at the route level.
   - For throughput (rps) guarantees tied to committed capacity, we propose a performance SLO: 95% of 1-minute samples meet the agreed rps/latency. SLA credits tiered: 5% invoice credit for a single month's miss, 10% for two consecutive months, capped at 25% of monthly bill.

3) Tenor / discount tradeoffs:
   - 12-month: standard list pricing, minimal discount, most flexibility.
   - 24-month: mid-tier discount (approx 12–18% off list), recommended if Aurora expects steady growth but wants a mid-term renegotiation window.
   - 36-month: deepest discount (25%+), recommended if Aurora is comfortable with forecasting demand and wants lower unit economics.

4) Ramp schedule (example):
   - Day 0 (start): staging buffer = 20% of committed capacity for 90 days.
   - Day 1–60: ~40% of traffic routed to Dedicated pool (validation stage).
   - Day 61–120: ~80% routed (scale validation).
   - Day 121–180: full production traffic.

5) Mid-term capacity increases: we can include a documented one-touch scale option allowing Aurora to increase base reserved capacity once per 12 months at a pre-agreed uplift percentage.

I attached a simple forecast template you can use to show expected ramp (Aurora_MA-Redwoods_Demand_Forecast.xlsx). If procurement prefers a 24-month with the ramp above we can propose concrete pricing and invoice cadence (monthly billing recommended for visibility).

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk procurement through the SLA wording.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Attachments: Aurora_MA-Redwoods_Demand_Forecast.xlsx (xlsx)

Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tenor and start-window — sizing & SLA tradeoffs

Team —

A few procurement/legal points from our side before we can route to Finance: 

- Invoice cadence: prefer quarterly invoicing for committed capacity, with a monthly metering statement for usage above committed.
- SLA credits: we need clearer caps and an escalation path. Can Redwood provide a draft SLA clause with exact credit calculation and an optional arbitration clause?
- Data residency: confirm that inference logs and metrics used for SLO calculations remain in the US region (we cannot have EU routing).
- Termination / early-exit: procurement asks for a mutual exit clause tied to material breach; they'd like to see a limited buyout schedule rather than full remaining commitment as a lump sum.

Cc'ing Marissa (commercial) to align on a customer-friendly path.

Procurement,
AuroraSoft
procurement@aurorasoft.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Reynolds <emma.reynolds@aurorasoft.com>, Procurement <procurement@aurorasoft.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tenor and start-window — sizing & SLA tradeoffs

Emma / Procurement —

Thanks for the detailed asks. Based on the technical and procurement notes above, here's a commercial path that balances Aurora's flexibility with predictable economics: 

Proposal (summary):
- Term: 24 months (compromise between flexibility and discount).
- Discount: 18% off list for the committed GPU pool described by Aditya.
- Ramp & start: target start date Nov 15, staging buffer = 20% for first 90 days; ramp to full production in ~180 days per schedule below.
- Invoice cadence: quarterly invoices for the committed capacity; monthly usage statements for bursts (billed monthly).
- SLA credits: tiered credit schedule as proposed by Aditya (5% monthly credit for one miss, 10% for two consecutive, cap at 25% of that month's committed invoice). We'll provide precise language and an arbitration flow; legal happy to consider a one-time mediation step before buyout.
- Early-exit / buyout: staged buyout schedule (month-by-month declining fee) rather than immediate remaining-term lump sum — we will put exact numbers in the term sheet.
- Mid-term scaling: one annual increase of committed capacity allowed at a pre-agreed uplift; additional scale options available on list prices.

Next steps:
1) I will draft a short commercial term sheet (Doc) reflecting the bullets above and post a preliminary DocuSign link.
2) If acceptable, we can set a Nov 9 call to finalize SLA language and invoice cadence so procurement can clear Finance.

Preliminary docs: Signed-MOA-draft.docx (attached); DocuSign (https://app.docusign.com/recipient/abcdef123456).

If this looks reasonable to you, Emma, we can convert to a formal commercial proposal and route to legal for the limited buyout language.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
